distinguishing_features: Uses a compliant elastomer coating that absorbs impact energy by extending contact time, rather than a pulsed chemical dosing schedule.
Mitigates the erosion failure mode passively via material mechanics (low modulus, high damping) rather than by chemically attacking a passive oxide film.
Applies to hydro-transport pipeline bottom erosion from sliding bed load, not electrochemical depassivation in an anodic cell.
Delivers a physical barrier/impact-absorber layer rather than an open-loop additive dosing and temperature setpoint change.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce particle-impact-driven material removal on the internal bottom surface of a hydro-transport pipeline without relying on increased surface hardness, so that peak contact stress stays below the damage threshold.
parsed.viable_reason: Compliant elastomer liners (polyurethane) are a known, physically feasible erosion-mitigation approach and the stated thickness and stress-pulse reasoning are plausible at the given scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Departing from the field's hardness/resistance paradigm toward impact-stress absorption via a low-modulus compliant layer is not a routine parameter change suggested by the closest prior art.
